title: Pedestrian crossing as a chart
summary: Draw the pedestrian crossing as a Sequential Function Chart with one step per light combination, and check that WALK shows only while the vehicles are red.
scope: Tests provide deterministic native POSIX host evidence only; they are not physical crossing, hardware, HIL, or certification evidence.
objectives: Turn the phases of a pedestrian crossing into the steps of a chart, each with an action that sets every light.
Leave the green step with a transition on the plant's request and move through the other phases with timed transitions.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/PedestrianCrossing.sfc.json the steps GREEN, YELLOW, RED, WALK and RECOVERY, their actions and the four timed transitions are drawn. Add the missing transition from GREEN to YELLOW that fires on PedRequest; the plant raises PedRequest from {{t:10}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Each step sets all five lights, so exactly one combination is shown at a time.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict the lights at {{t:0}}, {{t:20}}, {{t:40}}, {{t:60}}, {{t:90}} and {{t:110}} ms. A step shows its lights one scan after the transition that enters it fires.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:PedestrianCrossing.VehicleGreen=true,PedestrianCrossing.PedStop=true@0|green+STOP}} at {{t:0}} ms; yellow+STOP at {{t:20}}; red+STOP at {{t:40}}; {{v:PedestrianCrossing.VehicleRed=true,PedestrianCrossing.PedWalk=true@60|red+WALK}} at {{t:60}}; red+STOP at {{t:90}}; green+STOP at {{t:110}}.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press Check: The starter has no way out of GREEN, so the crossing never leaves the vehicle green; add a transition from GREEN to YELLOW whose condition is PedRequest.
stages.checkpoint: The visible scenario must pass with saved host evidence.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named PedestrianCrossingSfc and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:40}}, {{t:60}}, {{t:80}} and {{t:90}} ms: WALK shows from {{t:60}} to {{t:80}} ms and only together with the red lamp, and at {{t:90}} ms the red lamp stays on while STOP returns.
stages.checkpoint: WALK is never on together with the green lamp or with STOP, and the chart is back in GREEN at {{t:110}} ms.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Why does every action set all five lights instead of only the one that changes? Change the WALK action to leave VehicleGreen on and see which assertion fails.
stages.checkpoint: A step defines the whole output state, so no phase can leave a lamp on by omission. The scenario checks the logical sequence; it does not establish a physical crossing, real phase durations, HIL, or certification.

hints.text: A transition has a source step, a target step and a condition. The four timed transitions are already there; copy their shape for GREEN to YELLOW.
Add a transition with fromStep step_green, toStep step_yellow and the condition PedRequest.

faultCases: The starter has no way out of GREEN, so the crossing never leaves the vehicle green; add a transition from GREEN to YELLOW whose condition is PedRequest.
